context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It unifies care under a single provider while strictly enforcing regional data residency and compliance.

## Key Elements
* Patients (EU and US mobile/web clients)
* Licensed Clinicians
* Local Pharmacies (EU and US)
* Identity Providers (IdP)
* Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (with `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regional instances)
* AI Triage Engine
* GCP Global External HTTP(S) Load Balancers and Regional SFUs

## Relationships
* Patients and Clinicians interact with the Platform via HTTPS and WebRTC (DTLS-SRTP) using adaptive bitrate codecs.
* Platform connects to External Pharmacies via national e-prescription standards (EU) and HL7 FHIR APIs (US) using mTLS and payload-level digital signatures.
* Users authenticate via federated OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with Identity Providers.
* AI Triage Engine logs immutable inference records internally via Cloud Audit Logs.

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`): Chosen for regional isolation and compliance (GDPR/HIPAA).
* WebRTC SFUs & Global Load Balancers: Ensures video availability in degraded network conditions (<300 kbit/s).
* TLS 1.3, mTLS, and AES-256: Enforces strict data encryption in transit and at rest.
* Terraform & Cloud Build: Implements dual-region immutable infrastructure.
* Vertex AI Model Monitoring & Cloud Audit Logs: Provides traceability and immutable audit trails for AI recommendations.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional compliance (GDPR/HIPAA) by isolating data in separate GCP regions without direct cross-border replication. It simultaneously ensures high availability and resilience for rural users through edge caching and adaptive media routing.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring rural accessibility and regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA).

## Key Elements
- Patients and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
- External Identity Providers (IdP) and Local Pharmacies
- Regional GKE Clusters (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`)
- Node.js/GraphQL Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) Container
- Mediasoup WebRTC SFU Media Container
- AI Triage Service & Consent Manager Containers
- E-Prescription Adapter Container
- Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to API Gateway via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- BFF to Regional Microservices via gRPC over mTLS (Istio)
- E-Prescription Adapter to US Pharmacies via HL7 FHIR and to EU Pharmacies via national standards (REST/SOAP)
- WebRTC SFU to Clients via DTLS-SRTP
- Containers to Regional WORM Storage via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider utilizing `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for strict data residency.
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Container orchestration for regional microservices with CIS benchmark hardening and non-root policies.
- Istio Service Mesh: Manages mTLS, traffic splitting, and VPC Service Controls for network isolation.
- Node.js & GraphQL: Powers the regional Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) to abstract regional data formats.
- Mediasoup: WebRTC SFU container for video/audio streaming with sub-300 kbit/s bandwidth degradation.
- OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Observability stack for distributed tracing, metrics, and automated SLO monitoring.

## Rationale
Regional GKE deployments combined with Istio service mesh and VPC Service Controls strictly satisfy GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates without relying solely on application logic. Containerizing Mediasoup SFU with dynamic bitrate reduction guarantees resilient video and audio consultations for rural patients on unstable connections.

Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture uses a regionally isolated Istio service mesh to enforce strict data residency and regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Licensed Clinicians
- External Identity Providers (IdP) & Local Pharmacies
- Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway (Istio, Envoy proxy)
- Regional Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Node.js, GraphQL)
- Mediasoup SFU (WebRTC media server)
- Consent Manager & AI Triage Service
- E-Prescription Adapter & Regional WORM Storage (GCP Storage)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Istio Ingress Gateway: [HTTPS (TLS 1.3), DTLS-SRTP for video]
- Istio Ingress Gateway -> Regional BFF: [gRPC over mTLS]
- Istio Ingress Gateway -> Mediasoup SFU: [UDP / DTLS-SRTP bypassing sidecars]
- Istio Ingress Gateway -> Consent Manager: [gRPC over mTLS via Ext_Authz]
- Istio Ingress Gateway -> External IdP: [OAuth 2.0 / OIDC]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for regional data residency.
- Istio & Envoy: Manages multi-region traffic routing, mTLS, geo-restrictions, and rate limiting.
- Mediasoup SFU: Handles real-time video/audio streams with UDP/DTLS-SRTP.
- Node.js & GraphQL: Powers the regional Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) services.
- OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Captures distributed traces and metrics for observability.

## Rationale
Regional Istio deployments ensure health data never crosses jurisdictional boundaries, satisfying GDPR and HIPAA requirements. Edge resilience features, traffic prioritization, and direct media routing maintain low-latency video consultations for rural patients on unstable connections.

Backend-for-Frontend (BFF).analysis:
## Overview
- A cloud-native Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) built on Node.js and GraphQL, deployed across GCP regions (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`).
- Manages secure, resilient data aggregation and protocol translation for cross-border telehealth patients and clinicians.

## Key Elements
- **GraphQL API Gateway Layer (Apollo Server):** Handles query parsing, schema validation, depth limiting, and complexity analysis.
- **Authentication & Token Translator:** Terminates client JWTs, validates scopes, and issues internal mTLS tokens.
- **Resilience & Batching Middleware:** Manages query batching, optimistic mutations, and connectivity status for rural users.
- **Resolver & Aggregator Engine:** Orchestrates domain-specific data fetching and field-level authorization.
- **Telemetry & Audit Interceptor:** Injects OpenTelemetry context and regional audit headers for EU MDR traceability.

## Relationships
- **Clients -> GraphQL API Gateway Layer:** Sends aggregated queries and mutations over HTTPS.
- **GraphQL API Gateway Layer -> Authentication & Token Translator:** Delegates user session validation [In-process].
- **Authentication & Token Translator -> Resilience & Batching Middleware:** Passes validated operations [In-process middleware].
- **Resilience & Batching Middleware -> Resolver & Aggregator Engine:** Forwards batched requests [In-process function call].
- **Resolver & Aggregator Engine -> Domain Microservices (Consent Manager, AI Triage, E-Prescription):** Dispatches calls via gRPC over mTLS (Istio).

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js:** Core runtime for the BFF containers, managed via GCP Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
- **Apollo Server:** GraphQL framework providing schema stitching, query complexity analysis, and depth limiting.
- **gRPC over mTLS (Istio Service Mesh):** Protocol and transport security for all internal container-to-container communications.
- **OpenTelemetry:** Observability framework for distributed tracing and audit logging of AI recommendations.
- **Zod / Joi:** Validation libraries utilized at the GraphQL boundary for payload sanitization.

## Rationale
- Decouples client applications from regional backend complexities while enforcing strict data residency boundaries between the EU and US.
- Mitigates security risks and ensures high availability for unstable rural connections through robust middleware and resource governance.

Mediasoup SFU.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring high availability for users with unstable internet connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
- Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway (Istio)
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Node.js, GraphQL)
- Mediasoup SFU (Mediasoup WebRTC)
- Worker Pool (C++ / Node.js)
- Room & Signaling Manager (Node.js)
- Simulcast & Adaptation Controller (C++)
- Telemetry & Stats Exporter
- STUN/TURN Relay Agent (coturn)
- AI Triage Service, Consent Manager, E-Prescription Adapter, Regional WORM Storage (GCP Storage)

## Relationships
- Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway -> Mediasoup SFU: Routes video and audio streams [DTLS-SRTP]
- Room & Signaling Manager -> Worker Pool: Controls transport and producer/consumer creation [IPC]
- Mediasoup SFU -> BFF: Reports QoE telemetry and connection state changes [gRPC / WebSocket]
- Simulcast & Adaptation Controller -> Telemetry & Stats Exporter: Feeds bitrate and packet loss metrics [Internal IPC]
- Mediasoup SFU (Worker Pool) <-> STUN/TURN Relay: Relays media packets for NAT traversal [UDP/TURN]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Targeted cloud provider across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for data residency.
- Mediasoup WebRTC & Node.js/C++: Handles real-time video/audio SFU capabilities and low-bandwidth adaptation.
- Kubernetes with KEDA: Manages custom Prometheus metric-driven autoscaling for media workloads.
- Istio: Enforces mTLS, TLS termination, and API routing security.
- coturn: Provides NAT traversal for rural patients with restrictive firewalls.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates stateless media processing in regional GCP zones to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates. Custom KEDA scaling, simulcast adaptation, and STUN/TURN relays ensure resilient video consultations for rural patients under 300 kbit/s.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, EU MDR traceability, and resilience for rural users via GCP.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Patients, Licensed Clinicians
- **External Systems**: AI Triage Engine, Local Pharmacies, Identity Providers (IdP)
- **Containers**: Istio Service Mesh, GraphQL BFF (Node.js), Mediasoup SFU, AI Triage Service, Consent Manager, E-Prescription Adapter, Regional WORM Storage (GCP Storage)
- **AI Triage Components**: API Controller (Node.js), Consent & Policy Enforcer (OPA/Rego), Inference Orchestrator (Python/LangChain), Audit & Cryptographic Signer (Python/Tink), Fallback & Circuit Breaker Manager (Python)

## Relationships
- **BFF -> AI Triage Service**: Sends triage requests [gRPC over mTLS, Istio]
- **AI Triage Service -> Consent Manager**: Verifies regional permissions [gRPC]
- **Inference Orchestrator -> AI Triage Engine**: Queries symptoms [HTTPS / gRPC]
- **Audit & Cryptographic Signer -> Regional WORM Storage**: Writes signed logs [HTTPS, GCP IAM]

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Infrastructure**: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) ensuring strict regional data residency.
- **Networking & Security**: Istio for mTLS/AuthorizationPolicies, Google Tink for cryptographic log signing.
- **Backend & AI**: Node.js for API gateways and BFF, Python with LangChain for AI orchestration.
- **Policy & Resilience**: OpenAccess (OPA/Rego) for consent, custom async timeouts for rural fallback handling.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces regional data segregation to guarantee GDPR and HIPAA compliance while securing EU MDR audit trails via cryptographic signing. Additionally, circuit breakers and graceful fallbacks maintain platform availability for patients in rural areas with unstable connections.

Consent Manager.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using isolated GCP cloud infrastructure.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Licensed Clinicians
- Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway (Istio)
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Node.js, GraphQL)
- Consent Manager (Containerized Service with Go / Gin, OPA, Fallback Policy Cache, Break-Glass Mediator)
- Regional WORM Storage (GCP Storage with regional key rings)
- AI Triage Service & Mediasoup SFU

## Relationships
- BFF -> Consent Manager: Validates user consent and compliance policies via gRPC over mTLS (Istio)
- Consent Manager -> Regional WORM Storage: Persists encrypted consent records and audit logs via HTTPS
- Consent API Router -> Fallback Policy Cache: Reads cached local consent states via In-Memory / Local Disk
- Break-Glass Mediator -> Regional WORM Storage: Persists immutable emergency access justifications via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Ensures regional data residency for EU and US compliance
- Open Policy Agent (OPA): Evaluates dynamic GDPR/HIPAA compliance rules in real-time
- Go (Gin framework): Used for high-performance Consent Manager internal components
- GCP KMS: Provides regional envelope encryption for stored PII payloads
- SQLite: Powers the local fallback policy cache for unstable rural connections

## Rationale
Isolated regional deployments and OPA policy evaluation guarantee strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance while respecting data residency boundaries. Embedded fallbacks and break-glass mechanisms maintain availability and safety for rural or emergency scenarios without violating privacy constraints.

E-Prescription Adapter.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and resilient cross-border integrations.

## Key Elements
* Patients & Licensed Clinicians (Users)
* Local Pharmacies, Identity Providers (IdP), AI Triage Engine (External Systems)
* Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway (Istio)
* Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Node.js, GraphQL)
* Mediasoup SFU (Mediasoup WebRTC)
* AI Triage Service & Consent Manager (Containerized Services)
* E-Prescription Adapter (Containerized Service containing Prescription Router, Outbox Processor, Gateway Client, Status Notification, and Audit Logging components)
* Regional WORM Storage (GCP Storage)

## Relationships
* Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> E-Prescription Adapter: Transmits prescription requests [gRPC over mTLS via Istio]
* Prescription Router -> Outbox Processor: Enqueues messages [Internal Async]
* Outbox Processor -> Gateway Client: Dispatches queued payloads [Internal Event]
* Gateway Client -> Local Pharmacies: Transmits signed payloads [TLS 1.3, HL7 FHIR/REST/SOAP]
* Outbox Processor -> Status Notification: Dispatches delivery state changes [Internal Event]
* Status Notification -> BFF: Pushes status receipts and error codes [gRPC Stream]
* Outbox Processor -> Audit Logging: Forwards immutable event logs [Internal Async]
* Audit Logging -> Regional WORM Storage: Writes compliance logs [GCP Storage API, TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Target cloud provider for regional data isolation and compliance.
* Istio Service Mesh: Manages secure internal service-to-service communication via mTLS.
* Node.js / TypeScript: Core runtime for microservices and the E-Prescription Adapter.
* HL7 FHIR & REST/SOAP: Interoperability protocols for US and EU national pharmacy networks.
* GCP Cloud KMS with CMEK: Enforces regional encryption-at-rest key segregation.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data residency and compliance using isolated GCP regions and regional CMEK keys. It ensures fault-tolerant, reliable cross-border e-prescription delivery to unstable pharmacy endpoints via the Transactional Outbox pattern and Dead-Letter Queues.

Regional WORM Storage.analysis:
## Overview
A secure, cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, immutability, and compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
* Auditors & Compliance Officers (Secondary Personas)
* Local Pharmacies, Identity Providers (IdP), AI Triage Engine (External Systems)
* Istio Service Mesh & API Gateway (Istio)
* Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Node.js, GraphQL)
* Mediasoup SFU (Mediasoup WebRTC)
* AI Triage Service, Consent Manager, E-Prescription Adapter (Containerized Services)
* Regional WORM Storage (GCP Storage): Comprising Access Control & Policy Enforcer, Uniform Access Enforcer, Encryption & Key Manager Interface, Immutability & Retention Engine, and Lifecycle & Disposal Engine.

## Relationships
* BFF, AI Triage Service, Consent Manager -> Access Control & Policy Enforcer [mTLS/HTTPS]: Requests read/write operations
* Access Control & Policy Enforcer -> Uniform Access Enforcer [GCP API]: Rejects legacy ACLs entirely
* Access Control & Policy Enforcer -> Encryption & Key Manager Interface [Internal GCP API]: Applies regional CMEK for data at rest
* Access Control & Policy Enforcer -> Immutability & Retention Engine [Internal GCP API]: Applies WORM lock on write
* Immutability & Retention Engine -> Lifecycle & Disposal Engine [Internal API]: Triggers object purging post-retention expiration

## Technology Stack
* Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider for `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions ensuring data residency.
* GCP Cloud Storage: Used for Regional WORM Storage with Object Retention Policies in "Compliance Mode" for tamper-proof audit trails.
* Google Cloud KMS: Provides Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) with regional key rings.
* Terraform: Infrastructure-as-Code for automated regional provisioning and WORM activation.
* Istio: Secures data in transit using TLS 1.3 and mTLS.

## Rationale
The architecture uses strict regional isolation and GCP WORM storage to guarantee GDPR and HIPAA compliance while meeting EU MDR traceability requirements. Automated lifecycle management and uniform access controls balance strict legal immutability with cost efficiency and operational security.
